title: EvidenceManifestConsumerSubset v2
description: Development-only CP-1 typed evidence denominator. The criterion denominator is what this increment owes: the criteria frozen by the authored gate policies plus every acceptance criterion the canonical specification declares, and each one carries exactly one typed disposition, its own verdict id, and its own candidate-digest binding. The generated traceability index is a coverage map, not a source of obligations, and is not read. The deferred denominator is the deferred suites of the expected-suite registry; capability components are not a denominator source, so an exercised capability is never forced to declare itself unexercised. Gate-policy criterion keys, acceptance-criterion codes and suite ids each keep their own namespace.
$comment: docs/internal/DECISIONS.md D37 (gh#174): /v2 publishes evidence-manifest.schema.json's first incompatible successor. It drops the manifest-level verdict_ids roster and instead binds verdict_id and candidate_digest onto each criterionDisposition row, so a row's evidence is traceable to the exact verdict and the exact candidate digest that produced it, matching evidence_policy.candidate_binding: current_digest at the row level. /v1 stays committed, unedited, and locked to its own recorded shape digest by tests/contracts/evidence/test_evidence_manifest.py::TestSchemaVersioningDiscipline; this file is that same test's lock target for schema.const ctower.evidence-manifest/v2. title/description/$comment stay free to edit.

criteria.$comment: uniqueItems refuses an identical repeated row. JSON Schema 2020-12 cannot express uniqueness by key, so a repeated criterion carrying a different payload is refused by name at the criterion chokepoint in tests/contracts/evidence.

deferred_suites.$comment: minItems refuses an empty deferred roster while the expected-suite registry still defers a suite; uniqueItems refuses an identical repeated row. A repeated suite id carrying a different payload is refused by name at the deferred-suite chokepoint in tests/contracts/evidence.
